body: FOLLOW-UP CARRIER CHECK BEFORE EDIT: the ineligible ruling cannot be represented faithfully by the current public type. InductionResult.specificity is Map[DetailId, ScoreEstimate] and DetailAssessment.specificity is ScoreEstimate; Estimate has only Observed or Missing. MissingReason.Excluded would still be Missing, not Ineligible, and the chief explicitly ruled those are different. Omitting the map entry can encode ineligibility transiently, but assess must still construct a DetailAssessment and therefore currently invents a ScoreEstimate; skipping the entire assessment would also erase the discourse detail from independent address/AI-category axes. Specificity is not currently aggregated internally, so there is no hidden denominator implementation to fix; the public per-detail field is the consumer boundary. Proposed narrow typed carrier in interview: public enum SpecificityAssessment { case Ineligible; case Eligible(estimate: ScoreEstimate) }, used by both InductionResult and DetailAssessment. Episodic/Summary/OtherEpisode/Habitual/GeneralFact -> Eligible(Observed); literal Uninterpretable -> Eligible(Missing(Custom interview/classified-uninterpretable)); adversarial missing class -> Eligible(Missing(Custom interview/unclassified)); source unit absent -> Eligible(Missing(Custom interview/source-unit-absent)); the other discourse classes -> Ineligible. This preserves all other DetailAssessment axes and makes future coverage denominator unambiguous. It is new public vocabulary/API, so I will not introduce it without explicit ADR authority. Option[ScoreEstimate] is smaller but weaker: None carries no named meaning and nests applicability implicitly. Please authorize the enum shape or choose the alternative.
